transcript: A country where you find almost every  experience that you must have thought  of at some point in your travel bucket  list. On one side, mountains nestled  above the clouds and the world's  largest caves. And on the other,  crystal-clear beaches. World-famous  Vietnamese coffee, Asia's craziest  nightlife, the world's longest cable  car, or French-style cities, or the raw  history of the Vietnam War; there is so  much variety in this one country that  every day feels like you've arrived in  a new land. Welcome to Vietnam. Vietnam  is an S-shaped country located in  Southeast Asia that shares borders with  China, Laos, and Cambodia. It stretches  for about 1,650 km from North to South.  That is why, in a single trip, you get  to see cold mountains, tropical beaches , modern cities, and centuries-old  culture, all of it. Hey guys, this is  Shashank and welcome back to my channel . I hope you are doing absolutely good.  So, right now I am in Vietnam and I am  going to share a complete itinerary for  Vietnam that will be for 7, 8, or 9  days. In which we will visit Hanoi, Da  Nang, and travel everywhere, and in  this video, I will tell you how you can  come here. Which cheap flight you  should take. Where should you get your  visa from? How much will it cost? Where  can you stay? Where can you do shopping ? Where will you eat Indian food? I am  going to tell you everything in detail.  For children, pregnant women, and  senior citizens, what it's like, how  much you have to walk, I will talk  about everything in detail. And in the  end, I will also give you a budget  summary. So let's start our Vietnam  trip. Come with me. Now let's talk  about the best time to visit. Vietnam's  weather varies quite a bit between the  North, Central, and South regions.  Therefore, it is better to choose the  season according to the destination.  For North Vietnam, including Hanoi, Ha  Long Bay, Ninh Binh, and Sapa, October  to December is the best. For Central  Vietnam, including Da Nang, Hoi An, and  Hue, February to August is the best.  For South Vietnam, including Ho Chi  Minh City and Phu Quoc, November to  April is the best. And if you want to  cover the entire Vietnam, then the  period between October and April is  overall the most convenient and  comfortable. During this period,  exploring multiple regions in a single  trip is comparatively easier. This trip  has been planned through a company  called Way For Travel. So, if you want  their details, you can see them on the  side of the screen, and I will also put  them in the description below, and if  you are looking for a trusted partner,  you can consider them. So, first, let's  talk about how to reach. Traveling to  Vietnam from India is quite easy. From  Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, and Ahmedabad.  Direct flights to Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh  are available. There are three major  international airports in Vietnam.  Hanoi in the North, Da Nang in the  Center, and Ho Chi Minh in the South.  If you book flights two to three months  in advance, return flights can be found  for around 20,000 to 25,000. I booked  my return flight for 22,000, which also  included 15 kg of extra baggage. If you  want to travel on a budget, VietJet Air  is the most affordable option, and if  budget is not an issue, Vietnam  Airlines is the best option. If you  want to know how you can find the  cheapest flights, just type "flights"  in the comments. Now let's talk about  visa and travel insurance. It is  mandatory for Indians to get an e-visa  to travel to Vietnam, and the good  thing is that the process is quite  simple. Indian passport holders can  apply for a single-entry or  multiple-entry visa. Which can be valid  for a maximum of 90 days. And keep in  mind that visa-on-arrival is not  available for Indians in Vietnam.  Therefore, it is necessary to get an  e-visa before the trip. You can apply  for an e-visa online through the  official Vietnam Immigration website.  For the application, you mainly need to  fill in passport details, a  passport-sized photo, entry/exit dates,  and some basic information. If you need  any help related to the visa, please  comment "visa". I will share a proper  guide with you. Normally, the visa  processing can take around three  working days. But do not take the risk  of waiting until the last moment. I  would recommend that you apply for the  visa at least two weeks before your  trip. And one very important tip: apply  for the visa only through the official  government website. I will put the link  to the official e-visa website in the  description. After visa approval,  definitely carry a printout with your  passport because you might need it  during immigration. Now let's talk  about travel insurance. Travel  insurance is not mandatory for Vietnam.  But I personally would strongly  recommend it. Usually, basic insurance  costs around ₹ 300 to ₹ 800, which  is very useful in unexpected situations  like medical emergencies, baggage loss,  flight-related issues, or trip  cancellations. Now let's talk about SIM  cards and money exchange because a  little smart planning here can save you  a lot of money. Vietnamese Dong is used  for daily transactions in Vietnam.  Before exchanging currency, definitely  check the current exchange rate on the  screen. If you prefer to carry cash, it  is better to take USD. Instead of  purchasing Vietnamese Dong directly  from India, carry USD. Do not exchange  all your money at the airport. Only  exchange $ 50 so that you can manage a  taxi, bus, or basic expenses from the  airport to your hotel. Instead of  exchanging money at just one shop in  the city, compare rates at three or  four places. Besides cash, you can also  use forex cards, international debit or  credit cards, or neo-cards. ATMs are  easily available in tourist areas of  Vietnam, and cards are also accepted at  major restaurants, malls, and shopping  centers. Still, keep some cash handy  for emergencies. There are some UPI  apps that you can use in Vietnam. Write  "app" in the comments and I will share  its name. Now let's talk about SIM  cards. There is no need to buy a SIM  card directly from the airport because  prices can be higher. You can get a  local SIM from a Viettel official store , pre-book via Klook to pick it up at  the airport, or get an eSIM from Agoda.  You will easily find a SIM online for  400 to 500 rupees. Now let's talk about  stay options. In Vietnam, you can find  stay options for every budget. Just try  to book a hotel in the city center area  so that sightseeing, cafes, and markets  are easily accessible. Hostels are a  very affordable option for budget  travelers. Where you can get dorm beds  for 500 to 800 rupees per day. If you  prefer hotels, you can easily find  clean and comfortable double occupancy  rooms for 1500 to 3000 rupees per night . And if you need a little extra space  or a kitchen, Airbnb is a good option.  You can find fully furnished apartments  for 2000 to 3000 per night. If you want  a list of the best Airbnbs, comment " Airbnb". I will share the complete PDF.  So let's start with our Day One. Most  flights from India to Hanoi are late at  night and land between 5:00 and 7:00 AM . After immigration and baggage, you  should be out of the airport by around  8:00 AM. Freshen up at the airport,  connect to the free Wi-Fi, and exchange  around $ 50 into Dong for initial  expenses. Do not take a SIM from the  airport because prices here are three  to four times higher. After dropping  your luggage at the hotel, first head  to St. Joseph's Cathedral, whose  French-style architecture will give you  a Euro-vibe feel. From there, walk to  Hoan Kiem Lake and explore Ngoc Son  Temple. After that, definitely try the  famous egg coffee or coconut coffee at  The Note Cafe. After lunch, check into  your hotel and rest for two to three  hours. Make sure to go watch a water  puppet show in the evening. Where you  can experience Vietnam's culture and  traditions in an interesting way. Now  let's talk about local transportation.  In Vietnam, you get options like  self-drive bikes, Grab cars like Ola/ Uber, Grab bikes like Rapido, and local  buses. The most budget-friendly option  is a self-drive scooter, which costs  around 400 to 500 rupees per day. Local  buses charge 40 to 50 rupees, or Grab  bikes charge 100 to 150 rupees per trip . Grab taxis charge a bit more, but  they fit the budget. If you are  traveling with three to four people.  Exploring Da Nang by scooter is quite  easy and convenient. But there is a  common confusion here. Is an Indian  driving license valid in Vietnam? It is  mandatory to obtain an International  Driving Permit. Which is used along  with your Indian driving license. If  you also want to apply for an IDP,  comment "IDP" below. I will share the  link with you. Hey guys, very good  morning. Today we are going to Ha Long  Bay, and our bus has arrived. Let's go  and see how it goes. Hotel pickup  generally happens between 7:00 AM and  8:00 AM. Ha Long Bay is a UNESCO World  Heritage site. After an approximately 2 -hour drive from Hanoi, you reach Ha  Long Bay. There are basically two  cruise options here. One is a day  cruise, and the other is a two-day,  one-night cruise. On a day cruise, you  get activities like lunch, kayaking,  and cave exploration. The night cruise  has almost the same activities. But the  experience is a bit more relaxed and  luxurious. Because you stay overnight  on the cruise itself. However, the  price of a night cruise is almost 3x  more expensive than a day cruise. On a  day cruise, you first explore the Sung  Sot Cave. Where you get to see  beautiful rock formations with colorful  lights. After that, there will be a  bamboo boat ride or kayaking, which is  included, where you can enjoy limestone  caves and amazing natural views up  close. And then there is a stop at Ti  Top Island. Where you can swim and also  explore the island. After the cruise,  you will return to Hanoi in the evening . You are dropped off at your hotel by  8:00 PM. After freshening up at the  hotel, you can head out to explore  Train Street. Now let's talk about  language and local behavior. The  official language of Vietnam is  Vietnamese, and very few people know  English. So, be sure to download Google  Translate before your trip, as the  locals 'behavior and communication  style might be a bit different. So,  avoid unnecessary arguments. Deal with  things politely and just enjoy the trip . Keep day three for Ninh Binh. Now,  day three is optional. If you want to  go to Ninh Binh, you can. Otherwise, as  an option, you can also fly to Da Nang.  People also know Ninh Binh as the Ha  Long Bay on land. This is a full-day  tour. Departure from Hanoi to Ninh Binh  will be in the morning. Here, you first  get to experience the Tam Coc boat ride . Where local women row the boats with  their feet. It is quite a unique  experience. After this, you visit the  Hoa Lu ancient capital and explore  temples connected to Vietnam's ancient  emperors. If you like adventure, climb  the 500 steps of Mua Caves and enjoy  the amazing panoramic view of Ninh Binh  from the top. After completing the tour  in the evening, you get dropped off at  your hotel in Hanoi around 8:00 PM.  After freshening up, you can explore  Beer Street and do some shopping. Now  let's talk about food options. If you  are a non-vegetarian, then Vietnam is a  food paradise for you. Here you will  easily find seafood, chicken, pork,  beef, mutton, and many local dishes,  and that too on a very low budget. And  if you prefer vegetarian or Jain food,  then there is no need to worry at all.  You can find Indian restaurants in  every major city. Veg and Jain food  options are available there. Indian  food is a bit expensive. Like, for two  people, you will have to spend around  1000 to 1500 rupees. If you are staying  in an Airbnb, you can take basic  cooking essentials from India and cook  for yourself. If you want a list of veg  or Jain restaurants or an Airbnb guide,  write "Veg" or "Airbnb" in the comments . I will share all the details with you  in a PDF. Day four, today you have to  leave Hanoi for Da Nang. You can choose  a flight, train, or bus according to  your budget and convenience. Da Nang is  a beautiful coastal city in Vietnam.  After reaching the hotel, checking in,  and freshening up, head straight to  explore the Marble Mountains. Where you  get to see caves, temples, and amazing  viewpoints. Book your tickets in  advance. Because I took this package  from Way For Travel. So, all the  tickets and tours were already booked  by Way For Travel. My Khe Beach is  perfect to relax in the evening. Take a  walk on the beach. Enjoy the sunset and  just chill. Head to Dragon Bridge at  night. If it's the weekend, don't miss  the Fire and Water show here. For  dinner, you can try local Vietnamese  food. And if you want Indian food, you  can easily find Indian restaurants. Now  let's talk about senior citizens,  pregnant women, and kids. Vietnam is a  family-friendly destination, and with a  little planning, your trip can be very  comfortable. For senior citizens, the  Vietnam experience can be quite  comfortable. Just keep the itinerary  relaxed and use cabs to explore the  city. Places like Hoi An, Ba Na Hills,  Marble Mountains, Ninh Binh, and Ha  Long Bay caves involve some walking and  stairs in places. So wear comfortable  shoes and make sure to take breaks in  between. If you want a senior  citizen-friendly Vietnam itinerary,  write "Senior Citizen" in the comments.  I will share it with you. Now, talking  about kids, Vietnam is an amazing  destination for them. Theme parks,  cable cars, beaches, boat rides,  aquariums, and cultural shows. They are  going to enjoy it a lot. Just pay extra  attention to children in crowded areas  and when crossing roads, and always  wear life jackets during boat rides or  any water activities. Now, for pregnant  women, keep the itinerary a bit relaxed . Avoid unnecessary long travel and  enjoy the trip by staying in each city  for two to three days. Day five, Ba Na  Hills. Dedicate the entire day to  exploring Ba Na Hills. Where the most  famous attraction is the Golden Bridge.  Where you can see the mountain view  between the giant hands. Try to take  the 8:00 AM cable car because the crowd  is comparatively less early in the  morning and you can take comfortable  photos and videos. Definitely carry a  warm jacket because the weather on top  of Ba Na Hills is much colder compared  to Da Nang. After the Golden Bridge,  explore the French Village and Fantasy  Park. You will find many beautiful  photo spots here. If you want a  complete guide on what to explore in Ba  Na Hills, comment "Ba Na Hills." I will  share a proper PDF with you. After  enjoying the whole day at Ba Na Hills,  return to Da Nang in the evening, and  if you have time and energy left at  night, do explore the Da Nang night  market. Now let's talk about important  things to carry. Before starting the  trip, make sure to pack these things.  You can see the complete packing  checklist on the screen, and it will  also be in the description. If you want  this entire guide in PDF form, then  comment "Checklist" and I will share it . On Day Six, start your morning by  visiting Lady Buddha, a famous  attraction in Da Nang. From there, you  get a beautiful view of the sea and the  city. After lunch, Hoi An is just a 45- minute drive from Da Nang. You can also  easily reach there by renting a scooter  for around ₹ 400. Hoi An is a  beautiful ancient town. The yellow  buildings and colorful lanterns make  the entire town look very vibrant.  First, enjoy a coconut boat ride in Cam  Thanh Village and experience the  traditional Vietnamese boat dance, then  explore the Japanese Covered Bridge and  the local market where you can also buy  souvenirs. And as evening falls, make  sure to take a lantern boat ride on the  Thu Bon River. At night, the entire Hoi  An town looks so beautiful with  colorful lanterns that this experience  simply cannot be missed. Now, let's  talk about shopping options. There are  plenty of shopping options available  for both men and women in Vietnam, and  prices are quite affordable. There are  many international brand factories here , so you can find branded products and  apparel for very cheap. Just make sure  to bargain, as shopkeepers will  initially quote you three to four times  the price. If you need any help related  to shopping, comment "shopping". I will  share the complete PDF. Day Seven.  Today's next stop will be Ho Chi Minh  City. To reach here from Da Nang, you  have three options: flight, bus, or  train. Upon reaching the city, check  into your hotel. Freshen up. After that , head out to the Saigon Central Post  Office for sightseeing. If you want to  cover maximum places in less time, the  Hop-on Hop-off bus is the best option,  covering the city's major attractions  in about two hours. After this, visit  the War Remnants Museum, where you will  get a chance to understand the history  of the Vietnam War and its impact. In  the evening, sit at a rooftop café to  enjoy the beautiful skyline and sunset  of Ho Chi Minh City. Now, let's talk  about important apps. Before going to  Vietnam, make sure to install these  apps, as they will be very useful  during your trip. Reserve the last day  of Vietnam for the Cu Chi Tunnels and  the Mekong Delta. Go to explore the Cu  Chi Tunnels in the morning. Where you  can see how soldiers used underground  tunnels during the Vietnam War. After  lunch, head out for the Mekong Delta.  Where along with a boat ride, you get a  chance to explore traditional villages,  coconut factories, and rice paper  workshops. In the evening, return to Ho  Chi Minh City, rest for a while, and  then head to the airport for your  return flight. Now, let's talk about  drone rules. If you are taking a drone  to Vietnam, keep one important thing in  mind. To fly a drone here, you need  prior approval permission from the  Ministry of National Defence, and  foreign travelers also need a local  sponsor for the permit. If you want the  complete process on how to legally fly  a drone in Vietnam and how to get  permission, DM me "DRONE" on Instagram.  Now talking about the budget, you can  get a return flight from India to  Vietnam for ₹ 25,000 to ₹ 30,000.  Decent stay options are available for  ₹ 2,000 to ₹ 4,000 per day. For 7  days, it will cost around ₹ 18,000 to  ₹ 25,000. Food is quite affordable.  If you eat non-veg and can have street  food, it costs about ₹ 300 to ₹ 500  per day. But day tours, travel, and  sightseeing increase the budget  significantly. So, if you want a  hassle-free option instead of planning  it yourself, you can also consider a  package of ₹ 20,000 per person  excluding flights. Which includes stay,  transfers, and sightseeing, everything.  Now let's talk about the itinerary. If  you have 10 days, you can include Sapa  in your itinerary. If you have 13 days,  definitely include Phu Quoc, and if you  are coming for 15 days, you can  comfortably cover both Sapa and Phu  Quoc. If you want the complete day-wise  PDF of these itineraries, write " ITINERARY" in the comments. I will  share the complete PDF with you. I hope  you guys liked this Vietnam itinerary  video. And this time, I traveled with  Way For Travel. If you liked the video,  please subscribe to the channel and  like it. If you want to travel through  Way For Travel like I did, all the  details are appearing on the screen,  and I will also put the details in the  description. Thank you so much for  watching my video. See you in the next  video, in the next journey. Bye-bye,  take care.
